newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish police announce seizure of 240 kg heroin.
newsitem.headline: Turkish police announce seizure of 240 kg heroin.

text.p: Turkish police said on Tuesday they had seized 240 kg (530 lb) of heroin in the western town of Gebze, state-run Anatolian news agency reported.
Seven people, including one Morrocan and three Iranians, were arrested in raids on June 4 after a three-month operation, the agency said.
It quoted Adana police chief Mehmet Gundogdu as saying the heroin belonged to the rebel Kurdistan Workers Party against which Turkey has been fighting a separatist conflict for 13 years.
He said the heroin was on its way from southeastern Turkey to Istanbul where it would be shipped on to Western Europe.
Turkey is on the so-called Balkan route of drugs trading which is used to supply the West with drugs from Asia and the Middle East.
